clue.text: Ends message warning of motorway lights' failure

definitions.meaning: someone who finishes a letter or broadcast concludes with a farewell
read literally, the road signs are not lit up, switched off

explanation.definitionFit: To close a broadcast or letter is to sign off, and a notice that motorway signs are dead would say they are off.

clue.text: Foreman makes group-leader rage

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: rage means anger

explanation.surface: A supervisor makes the head of a team furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group-leader' looks like one person, but it means the first letter of 'group'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ganger is the supervisor of a gang of labourers, a foreman.

clue.text: Sunday best? That's a laugh!

parts.note: the cream of anything is its best part

explanation.surface: Someone mocks an outfit described as their finest weekend clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sunday best' looks like smart clothes, but splits into S and a word for the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something a scream means it is hilarious, a great joke.

clue.text: Existing on a diet? Anything but!

definitions.text: Existing on a diet? Anything but!

parts.words: Existing on a diet? Anything but!
parts.note: living by going without food might be read as fasting living, yet the phrase means a wild, indulgent life

explanation.definitionFit: A life of indulgence and excess is the opposite of austere dieting.

clue.text: Repercussion when retired engineer gets to house

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the engineer's letters are taken backwards

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for civil engineer

explanation.surface: An engineer, now retired, comes home and feels the consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: A repercussion is a reverberation or after-effect, as is a reflected sound returning.

clue.text: Heart-warming sounds of support

definitions.meaning: shouts of encouragement from a crowd

explanation.definitionFit: Something uplifting gladdens you, and supporters' shouts from the stands are applause and hurrahs.

clue.text: Where to apply stain remover instantly

definitions.meaning: literally on the mark or spot

explanation.definitionFit: Treatment goes right onto a spot, and an idiom for exact punctuality is the same phrase.

clue.text: A copper with little enthusiasm

parts.note: a copper coin is a penny, abbreviated P
petite means small

explanation.surface: A police officer with little zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman, but here it is the coin, P for penny.
explanation.definitionFit: An appetite for something is a keen desire or relish for it.

clue.text: Can't sort out what makes the difference

indicators.note: sort out here means put the letters in a fresh order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone admits they cannot resolve what separates two things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort out' reads as a verb phrase about resolving things, but 'out' signals rearranging the letters of CANT and SORT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A marked difference between things is a contrast, which is what distinguishes them.

clue.text: Many cheated in African country

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
to have someone is to trick them, so had means cheated

explanation.surface: A great number of people were swindled in an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Had in the sense of fooled is colloquial: 'I've been had'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a landlocked nation in north-central Africa.

clue.text: Thrashed for having made batter

definitions.meaning: whisked eggs and flour vigorously into a batter

explanation.definitionFit: Beat up means assaulted someone, and also whisked ingredients into a mixture such as batter.

clue.text: A people talented yet compliant

parts.note: men are people in a general sense
someone talented is able

explanation.surface: A gifted group who are also willing to go along with things.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone compliant is readily persuaded or cooperative, open to suggestion.

clue.text: French money made of silver

definitions.meaning: heraldic and poetic word for silver or silvery

explanation.definitionFit: The French word for money is argent, and in heraldry the tincture silver goes by the same name.

clue.text: Extravagant chairman has to tie things up

parts.note: a professor holds a university chair
to ligate is to bind with a ligature

explanation.surface: A wasteful company chairman is busy tying things together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chairman' suggests a company boss, but a holder of an academic chair is a professor.
explanation.definitionFit: A profligate spender is recklessly wasteful.

clue.text: Tour a Devon resort when transmission has ended

indicators.note: read as re-sort, sort again, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A trip round a seaside town in Devon, the English county, with a broadcast that has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like the seaside town but means re-sort, the anagram signal for TOUR A DEVON.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio operators use the phrase to signal that their message is finished and no reply is expected.

clue.text: See April produce displayed on trellis

indicators.note: produce here is a verb: make something new from the letters

explanation.surface: A gardener watches April bring a show of fruit trained up a framework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' looks like fruit and vegetables, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange SEE APRIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree trained flat against a framework is grown in this form, the word also naming the framework itself.

clue.text: First officer observed formalities

parts.note: proto is a prefix meaning first
COL is the abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: The senior officer noticed the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the code of correct procedure followed in diplomacy and ceremony.

clue.text: A sceptic acting so strangely

indicators.note: strangely says the letters are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A doubter is behaving oddly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds that God's existence cannot be known is a religious doubter.

clue.text: Got saffron to make such a dish

indicators.note: the letters given are used to make, by rearranging, a new word

explanation.surface: A cook has bought saffron to prepare a particular meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is the anagram signal here: the letters of GOT SAFFRON are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef stroganoff is a Russian dish of sliced meat in a sour cream sauce.

clue.text: Simplistic dossier about airman

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the file goes round the airman

parts.note: a dossier is a file of papers
AC is aircraftman, a junior airman

explanation.surface: A shallow report has been compiled on a pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: A facile argument is superficial, too simple to be convincing.

clue.text: It's clear the invalid is disheartened

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: an invalid under care is a patient

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a sick person has lost hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' looks like sad, but removes the middle letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent means obvious, plainly evident.

clue.text: Present cardinal to army corps

parts.note: HE stands for His Eminence, a cardinal's title
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A churchman is introduced to soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To be present is to be in attendance, at this place.

clue.text: Lawsuit in a court gets no-one's backing

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: split as no plus one, with one as I

explanation.surface: In court, a legal case finds that nobody supports it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but reverses NO plus I (one) to give ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action is a lawsuit brought in a court.

clue.text: Told to eat fish with Seville orange

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Told to eat fish with Seville orange', gives BADE round GAR, but nothing supplies the I of BIGARADE; a word such as 'one' seems missing and no source confirms the full clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Told to eat fish with Seville orange

clue.text: Urge to have fashionable name

parts.note: something fashionable is said to be in
to name someone, as in a document, is to cite them

explanation.surface: A push to give something a trendy title.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone on is to incite or provoke them to act.

clue.text: Tuning device is marvellous, I say

parts.note: something marvellous is magic in casual speech

indicators.note: say means spoken, so the letter is heard rather than written

parts.note: the first-person pronoun, said as the word for an organ of sight

explanation.surface: An excited speaker exclaims that something is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' reads as an exclamation, but 'say' tells you to hear I as its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A magic eye was a glowing indicator valve on old radios showing when a station was tuned in exactly.

clue.text: Left expert to make fine fabric

parts.note: an ace is an expert at something

explanation.surface: A departing specialist produces delicate cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lace is a delicate openwork textile, a fine material.

clue.text: Article appears after Tyneside writer takes drug

indicators.note: says the article is placed following the other pieces

parts.note: Tyneside is in the north-east of England, NE
a pen is something you write with
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A grammatical article follows a writer from Newcastle who uses drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the area round Newcastle in north-east England, giving NE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend a drug that brought forgetfulness of sorrow went by this name.
